title: Platform systems & services: dashboards, alerts, runbooks, roadmap, and team wiki (2026 Q2)
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates platform engineering guidance for the systems and services owned by Platform (eng-platform). It covers: operational runbooks, dashboards and alerting policy, on-call playbooks, recent retrospective findings and action items, and the near-term roadmap (Q2 2026). The intent is to provide a single reference for engineers, on-call responders, and stakeholders who run and evolve the Redwood inference platform runtime and control plane.

Key audience:
- Platform engineers (owners and contributors)
- SRE on-call rotation
- Product engineers integrating platform APIs
- Support and customer success for escalation context

1) Ownership and service inventory

Primary service groups (owners and primary contacts):
- runtime-api (owner: Runtime Team) — runtime-api-service, gpu-scheduler, kv-cache-proxy — primary contact: runtime-oncall@redwood.ai
- control-plane (owner: Platform Team) — config-store, routing-service, rollout-controller — primary contact: platform-oncall@redwood.ai
- telemetry-stack (owner: Observability) — metrics-ingest, alert-processor, trace-collector — primary contact: observability-oncall@redwood.ai

Each service has a single line service definition in the team wiki with: purpose, SLOs, dependencies, runbook link, and escalation path. Maintain that page when ownership or dependencies change.

2) SLOs and key thresholds

High-level SLOs (applies to hosted API and Dedicated control plane):
- API availability: 99.95% monthly (measured as 5xx and 4xx rate for production tenant routes)
- Median p95 latency for /v1/generate: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 250ms for short sequences (<=128 tokens) on Dedicated pools
- KV cache hit-rate: target >= 75% for steady-state workloads with prefix-friendly traffic
- Inference error rate (model decode errors / token): < 0.01%

Alert thresholds (examples):
- API 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes -> P1 alert
- API latency p95 increase > 3x baseline for 5 minutes -> P1 alert (investigate routing, scaling, kernels)
- GPU node OOM or nvml errors (any) -> P0 hardware alert and immediate paging to infra oncall
- KV cache miss surge (> 2x baseline misses for 10 minutes) -> P2 (performance regression)

3) Dashboards (recommended panels)

Standard dashboard layout per service:
- Overview (availability %, request rate, error rate, latency histograms)
- Capacity (gpu utilization per pool, memory, NVLink errors)
- Cost/throughput (tokens/sec, tokens/cost, batch size distribution)
- Cache & batching (KV hit rate, batch size percentiles, prefix reuse)
- Dependencies (db connection pool usage, network egress, downstream store latency)

Dashboard notes:
- All production dashboards must include explicit demo data ranges (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d) and an annotation layer for deploys and infra maintenance windows.
- Include a quick links section on each dashboard to the service runbook and recent incidents.

4) Alerting policy and workflow

Alert design principles:
- Prioritize actionable alerts and avoid noisy, symptom-level alerts. Prefer aggregated symptoms that map to runbook playbooks (e.g., "runtime degraded: high 5xx and p95 latency" rather than separate node-level CPU spikes).
- Use severity mapping: P0 (pager immediate), P1 (pager during business hours + slack notification), P2 (ticket + slack), P3 (informational).
- Attach runbook links and decision trees to every alert so first responder can follow steps without context switching.

Escalation workflow (summary):
1. Alert fires -> first responder oncall is paged. Acknowledge within 5 minutes.
2. Run quick triage using the service runbook steps (see section 5).
3. If not resolved in 15 minutes or if P0, escalate to service owner and infra oncall; create incident and set status page if customer impact.
4. Post-incident, assign a retro owner and link incident to the quarterly reliability board.

5) Runbooks: triage and remediation steps (template + examples)

Runbook template (top-level text to be included in each service page):
- Title, owner, pager contact, runbook last updated
- Symptom summary and how it presents in dashboards/alerts
- Quick triage checklist (commands, dashboards, logs to check)
- Containment steps (throttle routes, disable rollouts, switch traffic to fallback model variant)
- Remediation steps (restart service, scale replica counts, rollback deploy)
- Post-incident tasks (issue creation, tagging incident, add annotations to dashboards)

Example: runtime-api: high 5xx + p95 latency
1. Verify scope: use /health and production traffic filter to see affected routes.
2. Check GPU pool utilization and queue length (panel: capacity -> queue depth).
3. If queue > 2x normal and GPU utilization ~100%: scale Dedicated pool (increase replicas) or enable burst pool per autoscale playbook.
4. If p95 latency increased with low GPU utilization, check kernel failures and model load errors in runtime logs (log aggregator filter: "kernel-error" OR "kv-cache-fail").
5. If model variant is the cause, fail traffic to previous working model version using rollout-controller.
6. Document steps and mark incident for retro.

Commands and snippets (examples):
- kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=runtime-api
- rctl scale pool --name=dedicated-gpu-pool --replicas=+2
- curl -sS "https://control-plane/api/v1/rollouts/active" | jq

6) Retrospective (recent learnings and actions)

Recent incident summary (April 2026, partial kernel regression):
- Impact: 2 hours of increased p95 for several high-traffic routes; customers saw degraded UI responsiveness.
- Root cause: a kernel selection heuristic regression in the runtime that selected a slower fallback kernel for medium-length sequences under specific quantization profile.
- What went well: automatic fallback to a previous model variant reduced error surface; oncall acknowledged quickly and runbook steps were followed.
- Action items (owner / ETA):
  - Improve kernel selection unit tests to cover quantized medium-length sequences (owner: runtime-research, ETA: 2026-05-15)
  - Add an automated canary to QPS-weighted traffic for kernel changes (owner: infra, ETA: 2026-06-01)
  - Add dashboard annotations and a synthetic test for p95 under common sequence distributions (owner: observability, ETA: 2026-05-20)

7) Roadmap (Q2 2026 focus areas)

Primary initiatives planned for Q2:
- Unified alert taxonomy (reduce duplicate signals across telemetry-stack and runtime) — targeted rollout mid-May.
- Autoscale improvements for Dedicated pools (adaptive policies that consider sequence length and batch composition) — alpha by end of June.
- Cache eviction and warmup tracker (visibility into cold-starts for private deployments) — MVP May 2026.
- Team wiki consolidation: enforce runbook template across all runtime and control-plane services (owner: platform-ops).

Milestones and owners:
- May 15: kernel-selection unit test coverage (runtime-research)
- May 20: p95 synthetic test and dashboard annotations (observability)
- June 15: unified alert taxonomy rollout (platform)
- June 30: autoscale adaptive policy alpha (infra)

8) Team wiki and maintenance cadence

Wiki requirements:
- Every service page must include: purpose, SLOs, dashboard link, runbook link, dependents, last updated date, and primary/secondary oncall contacts.
- Quarterly review: owners must review SLOs and runbooks at the beginning of each quarter; record the review on the wiki with date and reviewer name.

Doc maintenance cadence:
- Runbooks: update within 48 hours after any incident where runbook steps were executed.
- Dashboards/alerts: triage noise weekly; reduce or adjust threshold if > 3 false positives in a week.

9) On-call playbook (summary)

First responder checklist (10 min):
- Acknowledge the page, set Slack status, and add initial annotation to dashboard.
- Run triage checklist in the runbook to identify scope and possible containment steps.
- Communicate in incident channel with clear status updates every 15 minutes until resolved.

Severe incident escalation (P0/P1):
- If impact is customer-facing and > 30 min unresolved: page service owner and infra lead, and prepare status page message draft.

10) Additional references and links

- Platform runbooks index: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-runbook-index
- Dashboard templates and Grafana panel library: /confluence/eng-platform/grafana-templates
- Incident postmortem process: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-guidelines

Appendix: quick checklist for new services
- Create service page in team wiki with required fields
- Add a minimal production dashboard (overview + capacity + errors)
- Define initial alert thresholds and link runbook
- Add SLO to SLO registry and set owner

If you have questions or need help aligning a service to this guidance, contact platform-ops@redwood.ai or join the #platform-ops Slack channel.
